pr.body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?
pr.title: Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing

raw_findings.body: WatchWriteEvents snapshots the latest resource versions when it is called, so the later watcher treats startup-time writes as already seen. A client subsequently watching from an older resource version never receives those events; deletions can be missed permanently.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The broadcaster has neither cached nor replayed events that occurred during the indexing interval.
raw_findings.impact: WatchWriteEvents snapshots the latest resource versions when it is called, so the later watcher treats startup-time writes as already seen. A client subsequently watching from an older resource version never receives those events; deletions can be missed permanently.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch moved initialization of the authoritative resource-event watcher until after search index construction.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Start the server watcher before the potentially long search initialization, as previously, or capture a resource-version boundary before indexing and replay every event after that boundary when the broadcaster starts.
raw_findings.title: Starting the broadcaster after index construction loses writes made during startup
raw_findings.trigger: With the SQL backend in an HA deployment, another instance creates, updates, or deletes a resource while this instance is building its search indexes, before this delayed call to initWatcher.

raw_findings.body: NewResourceServer returns no server handle while the initialized backend, cancellation context, database resources, and any already-started watcher goroutines remain active and cannot be stopped by the caller.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Failed construction leaves unreachable background work and resources running.
raw_findings.impact: NewResourceServer returns no server handle while the initialized backend, cancellation context, database resources, and any already-started watcher goroutines remain active and cannot be stopped by the caller.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new eager initialization path returns directly on error without unwinding partial initialization.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: On initialization failure, cancel the server context and roll back every completed lifecycle stage, including calling lifecycle.Stop when lifecycle.Init succeeded, before returning the error.
raw_findings.title: Constructor failure leaks partially initialized lifecycle resources and watcher goroutines
raw_findings.trigger: Lifecycle initialization succeeds, but search initialization or the subsequent initWatcher call fails, such as from a transient database error after search.init has already started its WatchWriteEvents goroutine.

raw_findings.body: NewResourceServer remains blocked because ctx is the constructor's private background-derived context and its cancel function is inaccessible until construction returns, preventing timely shutdown or startup failure handling.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation of the surrounding service startup does not interrupt resource-server initialization.
raw_findings.impact: NewResourceServer remains blocked because ctx is the constructor's private background-derived context and its cancel function is inaccessible until construction returns, preventing timely shutdown or startup failure handling.
raw_findings.root_cause: The eager blocking operation is tied to an internally created background context rather than a caller-controlled startup context.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept an initialization context through the constructor or ResourceServerOptions and pass that caller-controlled context to Init; retain the private server context only for long-lived watchers.
raw_findings.title: Eager initialization cannot be canceled by the startup caller
raw_findings.trigger: A database initialization, resource-stat query, or index build stalls while the enclosing application startup context is canceled or times out.

raw_findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex writes the map, which can produce a data race or a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic during startup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent watcher-driven index creation can crash the process while the initialization log is being assembled.
raw_findings.impact: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex writes the map, which can produce a data race or a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic during startup.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch invokes an unlocked cache traversal after enabling a concurrent path that can populate the same cache.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Acquire cacheMu.RLock for the complete TotalDocs cache traversal, or evaluate TotalDocs before starting the event watcher.
raw_findings.title: The new TotalDocs log can race with cache insertion after the event watcher starts
raw_findings.trigger: While TotalDocs is traversing a sufficiently large Bleve cache, the watcher started immediately above receives an event for an uncached namespaced resource and BuildIndex inserts its new index into b.cache.

raw_findings.body: Both builds can now create and populate the same file-backed Bleve directory concurrently, causing creation errors or inconsistent files; for memory indexes, callers can receive distinct indexes and the last cache assignment silently replaces the other one, potentially discarding an event applied to the replaced index.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A single logical index can have multiple concurrent builders and competing cache publications.
raw_findings.impact: Both builds can now create and populate the same file-backed Bleve directory concurrently, causing creation errors or inconsistent files; for memory indexes, callers can receive distinct indexes and the last cache assignment silently replaces the other one, potentially discarding an event applied to the replaced index.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch narrows locking to the final map assignment without preserving mutual exclusion for builds sharing the same cache key.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the removed global serialization with a keyed mutex or singleflight keyed by NamespacedResource, recheck the cache after acquiring it, and allow only different keys to build concurrently.
raw_findings.title: Removing whole-build locking permits simultaneous builds for the same index key
raw_findings.trigger: Two searches or a search and a write event concurrently observe a cache miss for the same NamespacedResource and both call BuildIndex.
